resolutionAlgorithm.step3: Apply each operation in order. Each 'set' names an EXISTING path whose current value must equal the operation's 'from' at EXACT JSON TYPE -- bool tested BEFORE int, because bool subclasses int in Python. A 'from' mismatch REFUSES the whole resolution.

resolutionAlgorithm.step5: The result is the resolved document. Its canonical digest must equal resolvedValue.sha256 below.

leafCensusOfThisDeltaFile.scope: every scalar leaf of retention-tiers.v28.json -- THIS DELTA FILE, not the resolved document. The resolved document's census is a different measurement and lives at $.derivedFrom.resolvedDocumentCensus.
leafCensusOfThisDeltaFile.method: a recursive walk descending dicts and lists. bool is tested BEFORE int, because bool subclasses int in Python and testing int first silently classifies every boolean as an integer.
leafCensusOfThisDeltaFile.whyThisIsTheLastMeasurementTaken: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 7.2.2 records FOUR measured instances of a self-report that measured the object BEFORE the self-report was attached to it, and is therefore structurally guaranteed to undercount by exactly its own size -- one of them committed by a document that was correcting the same class in an adjacent field. The repair is positional, not procedural: the only census that can be published is one re-walked from the written bytes AFTER the write. This block is written, the file is serialised, the file is re-read from disk, the walk is repeated, and the loop runs until the published figures equal the recomputed ones.
leafCensusOfThisDeltaFile.andTheRESOLVERRESULTIsPartOfTheFixedPoin: the acceptance test at $.resolverExecutionRecord is re-executed against the written bytes on every iteration, so the published resolution result describes THIS file and not an earlier draft of it.
